actions.justification: First step in any clinical encounter — must obtain history to characterize symptoms, onset, triggers, and relevant past medical history before initiating further workup.
Mandatory physical exam to assess for signs of heart failure (JVD, crackles, edema, S3 gallop) and hemodynamic status, guiding subsequent management.
Mandatory 12-lead ECG to evaluate for arrhythmia, ischemia, conduction abnormalities, or LVH that may be contributing to or causing the presentation.
Mandatory lab to assess renal function, electrolytes, and metabolic status in this patient presentation.
Mandatory biomarker for heart failure diagnosis and severity assessment.
Mandatory complete blood count to evaluate for anemia, infection, or other hematologic abnormalities.
Mandatory action: Chest X-ray is required within 60 minutes to evaluate for pulmonary congestion, cardiomegaly, and other cardiopulmonary pathology relevant to this heart failure presentation.
Mandatory action: TSH is required within 60 minutes to evaluate for thyroid dysfunction as a reversible cause of heart failure or contributing factor.
Assessing the hemodynamic profile (wet/dry, warm/cold) will guide diuretic and vasodilator therapy decisions in this heart failure patient with currently stable vitals.

Assessing LVEF is a critical next step to guide heart failure management, determine eligibility for guideline-directed medical therapy, and evaluate candidacy for device therapies (ICD/CRT). This is foundational to further management decisions.
Once LVEF is known, assessing ICD indication is important for sudden cardiac death prevention in patients with reduced EF heart failure per guideline recommendations.
Assessing CRT indication is appropriate in parallel with ICD assessment, particularly if LVEF is reduced and there is evidence of dyssynchrony or wide QRS on the previously obtained ECG.
NYHA functional classification is essential for guiding heart failure management decisions including medication titration, device therapy, and advanced therapy referral. Not yet completed.
Identifying structural abnormalities (valvular disease, wall motion abnormalities) helps guide etiology-specific treatment and is a standard next step in heart failure workup after LVEF assessment.
Evaluating candidacy for advanced therapies (LVAD, transplant) is appropriate as part of comprehensive heart failure management, particularly given the ongoing workup.

Patient appears hemodynamically stable with normal vitals. After completing initial assessment and diagnostics, checking optimal GDMT (guideline-directed medical therapy) duration and current regimen is the appropriate next step for heart failure management.

With stable vitals (HR 80, BP 120/80, SpO2 98%), cardiac rehabilitation referral is appropriate to assess eligibility and initiate structured exercise and education program as part of comprehensive heart failure management.
With HR of 80 bpm, assess whether ivabradine is indicated per guidelines (typically for HFrEF with HR ≥70 bpm on maximally tolerated beta-blocker) as part of optimizing GDMT.
Confirm whether the patient is on optimal guideline-directed medical therapy for heart failure, as this is a core management step after completing initial assessment and workup.
ACE inhibitor, ARB, or ARNI (sacubitril/valsartan) is a Class I recommendation for HFrEF to reduce mortality and morbidity. Should be initiated or confirmed as part of GDMT.

Beta-blocker therapy is a Class I recommendation for stable heart failure with reduced EF to reduce mortality. Patient is hemodynamically stable (HR 80, BP 120/80), making this an appropriate time to initiate or confirm therapy.

Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist (e.g., spironolactone/eplerenone) is guideline-recommended for HFrEF patients on optimal GDMT to reduce mortality and hospitalizations, and has not yet been initiated per completed actions.

Patient has been assessed for advanced therapy candidacy; initiating comprehensive transplant workup is the logical next step for patients with advanced HF who may be candidates for transplantation or MCS.
Evaluate need for inotropic support in the setting of advanced heart failure assessment, particularly if low cardiac output state is suspected despite current therapy.
